items.title: Analyserte krimbøker: – Romanen du skriver med KI, er ikke den samme som du hadde skrevet uten KI
items.excerpt: Aftenposten ran a stylometric analysis of Norwegian crime bestseller Jørn Lier Horst's novels before and after he began using AI: humming, 'during' and over a hundred times as many dashes — the language measurably shifted. Centre of Norway's biggest AI-authorship row. Off-list outlet (no on-list coverage of the Horst affair).

items.title: KI-bruk i bokbransjen: – Kan ikke nekte forfattere å bruke teknologien
items.excerpt: After accusations of extensive AI use by crime writer Jørn Lier Horst, author Hilde Østby says the Norwegian book trade can't ban authors from using the technology but must set rules — disclosure and labelling are on the table. Off-list outlet.

items.title: Risikerer vi at teknologien blir portvokter for litteraturen?
items.excerpt: Norway's writers' union Forfatterforbundet says publishers now screen incoming manuscripts with AI detectors and authors are being rejected as 'written by AI' when they say they used none — it demands clear criteria before an algorithm gatekeeps literature. (Debate piece; foro3d aggregated it 11-23.) Off-list outlet.

items.title: GlobalComix's pivot to AI is just muddying the waters
items.excerpt: Heidi MacDonald on GlobalComix's new Gemini-powered discovery feed, which pulls RSS content from opted-in comics news sites (ANN, CBR, ComicBook.com) into the app. Follow-up/analysis: the GlobalComix Gemini assistant itself was carded 11-20.

items.title: Can an Indie Author Make a Whole Cozy Mystery Series Look From an Image Model? My Cover Tests
items.excerpt: Hands-on test of making a consistent three-book cozy-mystery cover series, audiobook square and thumbnails with an image model (Nano Banana Pro API, book 1 as reference), with costs vs $400-900 commissioned covers and a disclosure/ethics section. Caution: names a specific API; check for advertorial tone.

items.title: Literary Translators Warn AI Threatens Their Livelihoods in Copyright Case
items.excerpt: The American Literary Translators Association and 11 other creative groups filed an amicus brief in Authors Guild v. OpenAI/Microsoft, warning AI translation could turn translators 'from interpreters into primarily editors of large language model outputs.' (OpenAI MDL amicus angle deprioritized; this is the translator-specific brief.)

items.title: AI Training is Copyright Infringement: What Publishers Need to Know about Thomson Reuters v ROSS Intelligence
items.excerpt: Publisher-side analysis of the Third Circuit ROSS opinion: the more an AI product is marketed as solving research tasks, the less transformative its use of STM content. Follow-up — the ROSS appeal ruling itself was carded earlier.
